issues.screen: Skip-Level Exam (and any quiz launched from a modal panel)
issues.route: home -> 'Ikuti ujian A2' -> modal 'Mulai ujian A2' -> quiz
issues.component: closeModal()+quizLoop() launch sequence vs FiezelBackNav stack
issues.issue: History/stack desync: starting the exam from its modal runs closeModal() (which calls FiezelBackNav.dismiss -> asynchronous history.go(-1)) and then immediately quizLoop() -> enterStage -> pushState. The async rewind lands AFTER the push, so the back-nav stack reports depth=1 (quiz layer) while the real history pointer sits on the base entry with no in-app entry beneath. Instrumented live: at '2-EXAM' snapshot stack=['stage:quiz:1'] depth=1, but ONE browser/Android back press mid-exam unloaded the app document entirely (URL -> about:blank) instead of closing the quiz. In the installed PWA this closes/exits the app mid-assessment. Because the document unloads, the quiz stage 'leave' hook never runs: abandonActiveSession/recordSkipExamFail never fire, so on relaunch levelTrust.exams={} — no failed attempt, no 24h cooldown. The back button is therefore also a free exam re-roll that bypasses the m025-177 anti-reroll rule, while the learner's in-exam progress silently vanishes. Same closeModal()->quiz pattern exists at app.js:4052 (levelEntryExam) and app.js:5735 (lessonSkipStart->startLessonSkipGate). app.js's own comment (app.js:3946-3951) names running dismiss() right before pushing a new entry as 'persis cara membuat riwayat dan tumpukan tidak sejajar' — startLevelExam does exactly that.
evidence: instrumented log: 2-EXAM {hlen:3,depth:1,stack:['stage:quiz:1']} -> 4-AFTER-BACK1 url about:blank; RELAUNCH {activeSession:null, exams:{}, lastSession:null}
issues.recommendation: Never pair dismiss() with an immediate pushState. Either (a) start the quiz stage from the modal's close callback after the history rewind settles (await one popstate/microtask), or (b) add a startStageReplacingLayer() in fiezel-back-nav.js that swaps the top 'modal' entry for the quiz entry via history.replaceState instead of go(-1)+pushState. Add a regression test that walks modal->exam->back and asserts the document stays alive and abandonActiveSession runs.
issues.concurrent_change_risk: none known (back-nav not in coordination/CLAIMS.json at audit time; repo is live)

issues.component: quizExit button, quiz stage leave hook, bottom nav during quiz
issues.issue: No exit confirmation anywhere: the '✕ Keluar' button fires go('home') immediately (app.js:6265, 6311), browser/Android back closes the quiz stage in one press, and the bottom nav stays fully visible and active during quizzes — one stray tap on any tab drops the session. All paths silently abandon the session (verified: sessionHistory gained {type:'grammar',answered:1,abandoned:true,reason:'quiz_exit'} with no dialog, no toast about lost progress). For level-exam and grammar-skip sessions the stakes are punitive by design: abandoning after >=1 answer burns the attempt and starts a 24h cooldown (app.js:1159-1161), yet that consequence is only mentioned in entry-modal fine print, never at the moment of exit. Accidental back-swipe or tab tap mid-exam = attempt lost without warning.
issues.recommendation: For sessions with answered>0, intercept Keluar/back/tab-tap with a lightweight confirm ('Keluar? 1/25 jawaban sesi ini hangus' — and for exams: 'percobaanmu terpakai, jeda 24 jam'). The stage close callback can return false and open the confirm modal, which back-nav already supports (close() returning false re-forwards the press).

issues.screen: Library, Skills Lab, Ask/Tanya FIEZEL, Writing, Classroom, Speaking+Listening
issues.issue: Six of the 14 valid views have no bottom-nav representation: when the learner is in Perpustakaan, Skills Lab, or Tanya FIEZEL, NO tab is highlighted (verified activeTab:null on all three), so the persistent nav gives a false 'nowhere' signal. These screens are reachable only through home-grid cards (or the header ask button), an IA the learner must remember; from e.g. Grammar there is no path to Library except back-to-home. Screen titles do compensate (each shows its own heading), so orientation is degraded, not lost.
issues.recommendation: Highlight Home as the parent tab when in home-launched sub-views (Duolingo pattern), or add these destinations under a 5th 'Lainnya/More' tab so the nav always shows a location.

issues.issue: Every tab press pushes one history entry with no de-duplication of lateral tab switches: after visiting vocab->grammar->reading->progress->home, exiting requires 6 back presses replaying every hub in reverse (verified BACK0..BACK4 chain, exit at depth 0). Android/Material convention treats bottom-nav switches as lateral (back from any tab -> start destination -> exit). A learner who has browsed tabs for 10 minutes faces a very long back replay before the app will exit; this reads as 'back doesn't work' on the Nth press.
evidence: live log: TAB chain depth 1..5 then BACK0-4 replay, BACK5 exit
issues.recommendation: Treat tab-to-tab moves as replace: if the top stack entry is a view entry whose fromView is also a bottom-nav hub, replace it instead of pushing (keep pushes for home->sub-view). Keeps 'back' meaning 'up', not 'undo every tab tap'.

issues.component: back-nav locked() gate vs empty history
issues.issue: The locked() gate (app.js:7630-7639) only defends against popstate events, but at fresh boot the back stack is empty and no sentinel entry is ever pushed, so there is no same-document entry beneath: the FIRST Android back press during onboarding leaves the app outright (verified: goBack from 'LANGKAH 1 DARI 6' -> about:blank). Step answers (name, goal, level) are only persisted at completion (fiezel-onboarding.js:186-200 markCompleted), so a learner on step 5 who reflex-presses back to 'undo a step' exits and restarts the flow from step 1. In-app the onboarding has no per-step back control either. Exiting at root is standard Android behavior, so this is polish, but a sentinel entry while onboarding is open (or per-step draft persistence) would make the gate's 'GERBANG WAJIB TIDAK BISA DITEROBOS' promise (fiezel-back-nav.js:29-31) actually hold on the first press.
issues.recommendation: Push one sentinel history entry when a mandatory gate/onboarding opens so the first back press hits the locked() branch (which re-pushes), and/or persist onboarding step drafts.

issues.state: reload at step 3 after typing name and picking a goal
issues.issue: Progress is NOT preserved on reload mid-onboarding. All step/goal/level state lives in closure variables; localStorage 'fiezel-onboarding-v1' is only written by markCompleted() at finish/skip. After reload at step 3 the user restarts at step 1 with an EMPTY name field — even though the name was already committed to app state (setLearnerName → fiezel-v4-state.userName fired on step 1→2). The user must retype their name and re-pick their goal. On a PWA that can be killed by the OS at any time, this is guaranteed repeated work.
evidence: features/onboarding/fiezel-onboarding.js:83 (STORAGE_KEY), :186-201 (markCompleted only writes at finish), :640-644 (typedName=storedName reads only the onboarding record), :165-168
app.js:4727 (onName commits name to state at step 1→2)
walkthrough log: pre-reload LS ob record = null, keys include fiezel-v4-state; AFTER RELOAD state = step 'name', 'Langkah 1 dari 6', name field value ""
issues.recommendation: Persist {step, name, goal, level} to the existing 'fiezel-onboarding-v1' record on every advance (done:false), and prefill the name field from state.userName when the record is missing. Resume at the stored step on next boot.

issues.state: user taps 'Mulai tes penempatan' on step 4
issues.issue: Tapping 'Mulai tes penempatan' does not show the test — it shows a full-screen 'Masuk ke FIEZEL' login gate (Lanjutkan dengan Puter / Lanjut tanpa akun). The 25-question quiz actually starts and renders BEHIND the gate (DOM check: quiz present, gate on top). The strongest commitment moment of onboarding ('I will take the test now') is answered with an account decision, and the user cannot see that the test is already waiting. Same gate also interposes on the 'Mulai Belajar' finish path.
evidence: app.js:3493 (pendingAfterGate==='placement' → startPlacement inside openApp), app.js:3497 (offerNotificationInvitation('after_onboarding') else armPuterAuthGate()), app.js:3619-3624 (afterOnboardingExit)
walkthrough log: layered {gate:true, quiz:true, appLen:11723}; after dismissing gate → '1/ 25 … VOCABULARY MEANING · 1'
issues.recommendation: On the explicit placement path, defer the Puter auth gate until the placement session ends (it already survives via pendingAfterGate-style deferral). Let the user land directly on question 1; offer the account after the result screen where its value ('keep this result on every device') is self-evident.

issues.state: brand-new learner, seconds after finishing onboarding
issues.issue: The very first home hero can greet a brand-new user with returning-user copy: 'Refa, Balik lagi setelah lama ngilang? Selamat datang, nggak ada yang nyatet.' selectLoginMessage() picks randomly from LOGIN_MESSAGES with no first-session / evidence filter, so lines about lost streaks, skipped days, and long absences can all appear on first contact — directly contradicting the personal bond the name step just built.
evidence: app.js:2874-2876 (pure random pick, only guards against immediate repeat), app.js:203 (the 'lama ngilang' line), app.js:4327 (hero-line uses it)
walkthrough log home text (reproduced twice in two fresh contexts)
issues.recommendation: Gate LOGIN_MESSAGES on learner evidence: if history is empty / onboarding finished <24h ago, use a dedicated first-day welcome pool ('Halo {name}, ini hari pertamamu…'). lastLearningAt() already exists (app.js:2870) to make this a one-line filter.

issues.component: auth gate + level-entry gate + tour + coach bubble stacking
issues.state: after 'Mulai Belajar' with self-reported level A2
issues.issue: The first 30 seconds after onboarding stack four competing demands: (1) Puter login gate, (2) 'FIEZEL LEVEL BELUM TERVERIFIKASI · A2' skip-level modal demanding 'Ujian Skip Level A2', (3) the 'Mulai dari Home' tour dialog, (4) a coach bubble. Worse, dismissing the exam modal with 'Nanti aja' silently DEMOTES the learner from their self-reported A2 to A1 ('Oke, kita mulai dari A1 dulu') — while onboarding step 3 promised the estimate 'akan disesuaikan otomatis setelah kamu mengerjakan latihan', not 'you must pass an exam or be reset to A1'. The promise and the reality diverge within one minute of making it.
evidence: walkthrough log: post-finish overlays {gate:true, skipLevelModal:true}; final home 'A1 · semua materi' + 'Oke, kita mulai dari A1 dulu. A2 nungguin kamu abis lulus ujian A2.'
shots/agent07-home-after-gate-390.png (BELUM TERVERIFIKASI · A2 modal over home)
issues.recommendation: Sequence the post-onboarding moments: one overlay at a time with the tour first and the account ask last. Align the level contract: either honor the self-reported level provisionally (adaptive evidence corrects it, as promised) or say honestly in step 3 that unverified levels start at A1. Never show the demotion as a surprise modal on first contact.

issues.state: user on step 2 or 3 wants to fix their name
issues.issue: 'Kembali' is hidden on steps 2 and 3 (topbar(false)); it only appears from step 4 onward. A user who mistypes their name discovers it in the step-6 summary and has no in-flow way back short of tapping Kembali three times from step 4+ — and back() itself supports going 2→1 fine, so the capability exists but the button is withheld exactly where a typo is most likely to be noticed.
evidence: features/onboarding/fiezel-onboarding.js:485 (carousel topbar(false)), :521 (goal topbar(false)) vs :543/:560/:589 (topbar(true) on 4/5/6), :807-812 (back() handles any step)
walkthrough logs: STEP2/STEP3 backVisible:false; STEP4/5/6 backVisible:true; back from 4→3 preserves goal+level (verified good)

issues.issue: Step 5's title is a question the user cannot answer: 'Kapan kamu ingin belajar?' has no input, no choice, nothing tappable except 'Lanjut' — the body then explains the system decides. Additionally it asserts 'Notifikasi belajar: Aktif' and the step-6 summary shows 'Pengingat: Aktif' before any browser notification permission exists (the permission ask comes later, if at all). The copy claims a state that is not yet true.
evidence: features/onboarding/fiezel-onboarding.js:566-568 (question title + 'Notifikasi belajar: Aktif'), :604 ('Pengingat Aktif' summary row)
walkthrough log: notifPanel:false after finish (no permission prompt had occurred)
issues.recommendation: Retitle step 5 as a statement ('Pengingat belajar: aku yang atur waktunya') and phrase the status honestly ('Pengingat: menunggu izin notifikasi' until permission is granted).

issues.issue: Two consecutive steps ask nearly the same question: step 3 asks 'Berapa perkiraan level bahasa Inggrismu sekarang?' (CEFR chips) and step 4's title is 'Apa level bahasa kamu?'. The user just answered that. Step 4 is actually about the placement TEST — its title mislabels the step and makes the flow feel repetitive, and the stepper label 'Level' on step 4 compounds it (the level chips live in step 3, labeled 'Tujuan').
issues.recommendation: Retitle step 4 to the action it contains ('Ukur level kamu — tes penempatan') and rename its stepper label to 'Tes'.

issues.state: name >24 UTF-16 units containing emoji at an odd offset
issues.issue: normalizeName() truncates with slice(0,24) on UTF-16 code units, which can split a surrogate pair: input 'A'+20 emoji yields 'A😀😁😂🤣😃😄😅😆😇😉😊\ud83d' — a lone surrogate rendered as '�' in every greeting, the document title, and push notifications. The browser's maxlength=24 happens to protect the typing path (our fill produced a safe 23-unit value), but the slice runs on every other entry path (backup restore, settings, stored records), so the corruption is reachable.
evidence: Node repro: normalizeName('A'+20 emoji) → ends with lone \ud83d, /[\uD800-\uDBFF]$/ test true, renders 'A😀…😊�'
browser check: maxlength kept input at 23 safe units (shots/agent07-step1-emoji-390.png, shots/agent07-step6-summary-390.png show intact emoji name flowing through summary)
issues.recommendation: Truncate on code points: Array.from(clean).slice(0,NAME_MAX).join('') (or strip a trailing lone surrogate after slice).

issues.issue: At 320x568 the mandatory name step does not fit: the 'Lanjut' button bottom sits at y≈762 vs a 568px viewport (sheet scrollHeight 799). The name input itself is at the fold edge, so the first required action needs a scroll, and once the soft keyboard opens (~260px) the input/CTA region shrinks further. No horizontal overflow (good), but the one step that cannot be skipped is the one that overflows most.
evidence: style.css:1340 (.fiezel-ob overflow-y:auto — scrolling works, content is reachable)
issues.recommendation: At small heights, shrink the mascot stage (--fz-ob-paw is already a CSS var, clamp it by vh) and/or collapse the greet bubble so input+CTA fit in the first viewport.

issues.issue: The final step offers three exits — 'Mulai Belajar' (primary), a ghost 'Lewati' below it, and 'Lewati' in the top bar — and all three end onboarding at the same place (home). Two 'skip' labels on a step where there is nothing left to skip read as 'there is more I can avoid', and dilute the single celebratory CTA.
evidence: features/onboarding/fiezel-onboarding.js:607-608 (primary + ghost step-skip), :853 (step-skip at LAST_STEP === finish('skip')), :65-69 (top-right Lewati on every step except 1)
issues.recommendation: On step 6, drop both 'Lewati' buttons and keep only 'Mulai Belajar'.

issues.issue: The splash occupies essentially the entire first 5 seconds (removed at ~5.2s in our runs; brief says 6-9s is possible). Within 5s the user has seen brand identity (wordmark, mascot, 'Adaptive English') but has had zero interactive contact and zero product understanding beyond the name. Milestone met only at its edge; on slower devices the 5s snapshot would still be the dark splash.
evidence: shots/agent07-t5s-390.png (step 1 already visible at 5.0s in this run)
issues.recommendation: Keep the choreography but cap total splash at ~3.5-4s on first run so step 1 is guaranteed inside the 5-second window on mid-range hardware. (Splash internals are Agent 01/brand scope; flagged here only for the milestone.)

issues.issue: After tapping 'Dengarkan', the note shows 'Memutar…' and ALL answer options AND the Dengarkan button stay disabled until audio.play() settles. There is no watchdog timeout: in the test environment the lock persisted >9.5s with no way forward except 'Keluar'. The fallback unlock (note + unlock()) only runs when the promise resolves/rejects (app.js:6334-6348); a hanging TTS fetch = student trapped on the question. UNVERIFIED whether owner's device/network ever hangs this long, but the code has no guard.
issues.recommendation: Wrap audio.play() in Promise.race with a ~8-10s timeout that re-enables Dengarkan, unlocks options, and sets the honest 'Suaranya belum berbunyi' note (same copy as the existing failure branch).
issues.concurrent_change_risk: T-026 (features/neural-voice claimed by another agent — coordinate before touching audio ladder)

issues.issue: One tap on 'Keluar' (or any bottom-nav tab, which stays visible and active during the quiz) abandons a 25-question session instantly: no confirmation, no resume. Re-entering the lesson restarts at 1/25 with the IDENTICAL first questions (preserveOrder:true), so an accidental tap costs the whole session and forces repeating already-answered items. Answer evidence is kept (history/mastery recorded per answer, session logged abandoned:true), so no data loss — but the UX cost of a stray tap on a long session is high.
evidence: evidence/agent08-run-a.json (after-exit: abandoned:true, answered:2; reenter: prog '1/ 25', same question '___ name is Sari.')
issues.recommendation: Confirm exit when >=1 answer given ('Sudah 3 soal terjawab — yakin keluar?'), and/or persist remaining-question queue in state.activeSession to offer resume.

issues.issue: The pembahasan panel is written below options and the app never scrolls to it: measured feedback top at y=796 of an 844px viewport in grammar (only ~48px visible) and y=675 in vocab. The verdict is mitigated by the confidence popup, but the actual explanation — the learning payload — requires a manual scroll the UI never hints at; 'Lanjut' meanwhile sits in the sticky topbar at the top, so the eye bounces bottom-to-top every question. Only the retry tutorTurn path calls scrollIntoView (app.js: speak(), retry branch).
issues.recommendation: After reveal, f.scrollIntoView({block:'start'}) behind the same prefers-reduced-motion gate already used for tutorTurn.

issues.issue: Cloze reveal order contradicts the MCQ path: revealCloze paints the full pembahasan FIRST, then opens the confidence popup ON TOP of it (app.js:6533-6547), while the MCQ path was deliberately reordered (R2-5) to popup -> analyzing -> clean reveal (app.js:6497-6499). The popup's 'Lewati, langsung ke pembahasan' label is false here — the pembahasan is already behind the scrim. Cloze also skips the ANALYZING pause entirely, so the loop feels different between question types.
evidence: app.js:6533-6547 (revealCloze: feedback painted, answer.locked=true, then openConfidencePop)
issues.recommendation: Route cloze through the same confidencePopThen -> showCoreAnalyzing -> reveal sequence as MCQ.

issues.issue: After a wrong first attempt and a wrong second attempt, TWO options carry the identical red 'PILIHANMU' badge with nothing distinguishing the first try from the assessed final answer. The feedback text names the final answer, but the option list itself is ambiguous about which 'your choice' counted.
evidence: shots/agent08-12-q2-feedback-wrong.png (both 'She name is Sari.' and 'Hers name is Sari.' badged PILIHANMU)
app.js:6441 (button.classList.add on every attempt, never differentiated)
issues.recommendation: Label the first attempt differently (e.g. 'PERCOBAAN 1') or dim it, keeping 'PILIHANMU' only on the final answer.

issues.issue: A grammar lesson is 25 questions (GRAMMAR_SESSION_SIZE=25) with only a numeric 'n / 25' counter — no progress bar — and every question costs ~3 interactions (answer -> confidence popup choice or Lewati -> 'Lihat pembahasan' -> 700ms ANALYZING -> scroll to read -> 'Lanjut'). That is 75+ taps and ~25 forced 700ms pauses per lesson. The pedagogy is deliberate (SRL confidence capture), but the ceremony weight on a 25-item mobile session is heavy and the counter alone gives weak sense of progress.
issues.recommendation: Add a thin visual progress bar under the topbar; let 'setConfidence' auto-continue to pembahasan (drop the extra 'Lihat pembahasan' tap); consider chunking 25 into visible sets of 5.

issues.issue: Typo tolerance forgives edit-distance 1, but a transposition ('gose' for 'goes' — the most common typing slip) counts as distance 2 in plain Levenshtein and is graded WRONG with the full misconception flow. Minor grading-UX mismatch with the stated 'typo is not evidence of misconception' philosophy.
issues.recommendation: Use Damerau-Levenshtein (transposition = distance 1) in the production grader.

issues.issue: Progress counter renders with uneven spacing: '1/ 25' (space after slash only) from '${asked+1}/ ${planned}'. Cosmetic.
issues.recommendation: Render '1 / 25'.

issues.screen: Ujian Skip Level / Tes Kemampuan Dasar (quiz loop)
issues.state: during exam, after each answered question
issues.issue: CRITICAL CHECK FAILED: assessments reveal correctness AND the correct answer after every question, mid-test, including exam mode. On tap, answer() adds classList 'correct'/'wrong' to the chosen option in ALL modes (app.js:6441 button.classList.add(ok?'correct':'wrong')) and fires answerFeedbackSignal (haptic+sound+'Benar!/Belum tepat' burst, app.js:2542-2546). The confidence popup then announces the verdict (app.js:1279). reveal() then highlights the correct option (app.js:6392 querySelectorAll('.option')[q.answerIndex].classList.add('correct')) and prints 'Jawaban yang paling tepat adalah <correct>' with full explanation, per-distractor breakdown and an AI-explain button (app.js:6395-6396). cfg.noHints only disables retry/hints (app.js:6486-6493), NOT the reveal. Verified live in exam mode: tap classes ['option correct','option','option','option'], feedback 'Jawaban yang paling tepat adalah students who collect plastic on a beach'. Because the exam draws from a finite per-level bank ('Soal diacak dari bank level A2 setiap percobaan') and retry costs only 24h (app.js:100-103,991), an examinee can farm the answer key across attempts — undermining the stated contract 'Jawab benar minimal 80% tanpa petunjuk' (app.js:126) and the verified-level trust chain. Same channel applies to placement (retake after 24h, app.js:6178).
issues.recommendation: In measurement modes (placement, level-exam, grammar-skip): suppress per-question verdict, burst, option highlight and explanation; keep answers neutral ('tersimpan, lanjut') and move the full per-item review (correct answers + explanations + AI button) to the post-result screen. If per-item feedback is a deliberate pedagogy choice, at minimum stop revealing the correct option text/highlight during exams.
issues.concurrent_change_risk: none observed on quiz pipeline; m025-177 skip-integrity release touched adjacent exam code

issues.issue: Exiting an exam mid-test silently burns the attempt: 'Keluar' (and back gesture / bottom nav) triggers abandonActiveSession which records a FAIL (score 0/25, accuracy 0) plus 24h cooldown with weakSkill 'ujian ditinggalkan sebelum selesai' (app.js:1161, recordSkipExamFail app.js:987-993) — with NO confirmation dialog and NO message at exit time (quizExit handler just go('home'), app.js:6313; enterStage leave app.js:6559; no confirm() anywhere). Verified live: after tapping Keluar with 1 answer, state.levelTrust.exams.A2={attempts:1,passed:false,cooldownUntil:+24h} and the screen showed only the home view. The instructions modal never warns that exiting counts as a failed attempt — the user discovers the penalty only when reopening the panel ('Percobaan terakhir: 0/25 (0%) · yang menjatuhkan: ujian ditinggalkan sebelum selesai' + disabled 'Bisa diulang 24 jam lagi').
issues.recommendation: Add an exit-confirmation dialog in exam/skip-gate mode ('Keluar sekarang dihitung gagal dan ujian terkunci 24 jam. Tetap keluar?') and state the rule in the exam instructions modal. Show a toast after abandonment explaining what was recorded.
issues.concurrent_change_risk: m025-177 introduced this penalty deliberately (anti-reroll); coordinate before changing semantics — but the missing WARNING is purely additive

issues.issue: Penalty inconsistency / integrity loophole: killing or reloading the app mid-exam escapes the fail+cooldown entirely. The boot-time path in sanitizeState closes a dangling activeSession as abandoned 'interrupted' but never calls recordSkipExamFail (app.js:1030), unlike the in-app exit path (app.js:1161). Verified live: answered=1 persisted to storage, page reloaded → sessionHistory got {type:'level-exam',answered:1,abandoned:true,reason:'interrupted'} and levelTrust.exams.A2 remained null (no attempt, no cooldown). Net effect: the honest user who taps 'Keluar' is punished 24h; the user who swipes the PWA away gets a free reroll — the exact 'open, peek at questions, bail' behavior m025-177 says it closed (with per-question answers also revealed per 09-001).
issues.recommendation: Apply the same measurement-abandon rule in the boot path: if the interrupted session is type level-exam/grammar-skip with answered>0, record the fail/cooldown there too (or, better, drop the punitive model and make both paths resume-able).
issues.concurrent_change_risk: m025-177 skip-integrity work is active in this exact area (coordination/CLAIMS.json)

issues.issue: No resume: mid-test progress is lost silently. A placement (~10 min, 25 soal) or exam interrupted at question 24 restarts from zero with a fresh shuffled set; on return the app shows home with no notice that a test was in progress or lost (verified after both Keluar and reload — no 'lanjutkan tes' offer, no message; placementDone stays false, answers only land in analytics history). Loss is by design for measurement integrity, but it is never communicated to the user at exit or on return.

The static splash's 15s watchdog (index.html:125-134) then removes the splash, leaving a permanently BLANK main area: header and bottom nav render and look alive, but #app stays empty forever — no loading indicator, no error, no retry. Tapping nav during this state renders misleading fake-empty hubs: Vocabulary Hub claims '0 kata level A1' because V is still empty, presenting missing data as a content-less level.
issues.recommendation: Wrap the required DATA fetches in a timeout (e.g. AbortSignal.timeout(20000)) so stalls fall into the existing error path; while load() is pending, render a loading state (the shipped-but-unused SkeletonHelpers would fit) in #app and gate nav-rendered hubs on 'banks loaded' instead of showing 0-counts.

issues.state: bank JSON fetch fails (network error / server 4xx-5xx)

Jalankan melalui server lokal/GitHub Pages, bukan file://.' — a raw English fetch error injected into an Indonesian UI, plus advice about file:// that is wrong/misleading for the actual cause (network failure or server error) on an installed PWA. There is no 'Coba lagi' retry button, no offline detection (navigator.onLine), and the bottom nav stays interactive, leading to the same misleading fake-empty hubs as 16-001.
issues.recommendation: Branch the message: navigator.onLine===false → 'Kamu sedang offline…', HTTP status → 'Server bermasalah…', keep file:// hint only for location.protocol==='file:'. Add a primary 'Coba lagi' button that re-runs load() instead of requiring a manual reload.

issues.state: device offline when a question is submitted

The CF transport checks navigator.onLine after a network error (app.js:7425-7429, aiTaskError 'ai_offline') but the Puter path (askPuterAI, app.js:7403-7411) has no onLine check and no fast-fail, so the default deployment waits 30s with no cancel button while related-material results sit below it.

issues.issue: The quiz 'Keluar' button exits instantly — onclick goes straight to go('home') with no confirmation (app.js:6265). issues.state: warm launch, SW fully cached (daily open)

A ~4.2 s brand hold on every daily open is the app's largest fixed perceived-latency cost; nothing the network layer does can reduce it.

issues.issue: Bottom-nav taps take 401–783 ms from click to newly-rendered content frame (two runs: vocab 448/783, grammar 502/544, reading 502/593, progress 401/497, home 454/496 ms) — on localhost with a desktop CPU. Every navigation destroys and rebuilds the whole view via innerHTML (renderInner), re-runs enhanceUI, and wraps it in document.startViewTransition, producing 50–380 ms long tasks per tap. On the owner's phone (~4x slower CPU) this lands well over the ~300 ms 'sluggish' threshold on every tab switch.
issues.recommendation: Cache rendered view DOM (or use per-view containers toggled by display) so tab switches don't re-parse innerHTML; run enhanceUI incrementally; keep startViewTransition but ensure the swap callback stays <100 ms.

issues.issue: Long-task profile at boot: unthrottled 4 tasks totaling 1,063 ms (max 784 ms at t=1.3 s); at 4x CPU throttle 21 tasks totaling 5,590 ms (max 2,105 ms) — i.e., on a mid-range phone the main thread is blocked ~5.6 s during boot, freezing splash animation frames and delaying interactivity. Drivers: evaluating 64 script files (2.08 MB) and JSON.parse of ~6 MB of banks on the main thread.
evidence: evidence/a17-loads.json (cold_unthrottled longtasks; cold_throttled longtasks n=21 total=5590 max=2105)
issues.recommendation: Same fix family as 17-001: shrink/split banks, parse in a Worker, and bundle the 64 boot scripts into fewer files to cut eval overhead.

issues.state: two tabs open on the same origin
issues.issue: Two tabs each loaded state at totalAnswered=30; each answered 1 question (2 total). Final localStorage: totalAnswered=31 — one answer silently lost to last-writer-wins. No 'storage' event listener exists anywhere in the codebase (grep for addEventListener('storage') returns nothing), so tabs never learn about each other's writes. A learner with the PWA open plus a browser tab will silently lose progress from one of them.
evidence: app.js:1072 (saveFlushWrite unconditional localStorage.setItem, no revision check against stored value)
tmp-20-t25 stdout: tab1 {mem:31,rev:8} tab2 {mem:31,rev:8}, final 31 after 2 distinct answers
issues.recommendation: Add a storage-event listener that reloads or merges when stateRevision in localStorage is newer than in memory; or refuse to clobber when stored stateRevision > in-memory revision.

issues.state: hostile userName injected directly into fiezel-v4-state (restore/sync path)
issues.issue: sanitizeState does not clamp or normalize userName, so a 200-char name arriving via state restore (Puter sync, manual import) bypasses the UI's maxlength=24 and normalizeName. Result: 5 overflowing elements, the ritual card 'Mulai' button pushed fully off-screen. RTL/bidi-override (U+202E) and zalgo names persist unnormalized with no dir=auto/bidi isolation on render sites. XSS is NOT possible (verified pass) — this is layout/spoofing only.
evidence: app.js:24-31 (setLearnerName normalizes, but only on the UI path)
issues.recommendation: Run userName through normalizeName inside sanitizeState (defense in depth) and add dir=auto or bidi isolation (FSI/PDI) at name render sites.

issues.state: programmatic callers (sync, notifications) with emoji-heavy names
issues.issue: normalizeName ends with .slice(0,24) on UTF-16 code units, splitting surrogate pairs. Verified in-page: normalizeName('A'+'😀'.repeat(20)) returns a string ending in lone high surrogate 0xd83d, and encodeURIComponent() on it throws 'URI malformed'. Unreachable via the UI (input maxlength truncates first — verified) but reachable via programmatic paths that slice names (app.js:3249 remoteActivitySnapshot, app.js:3255 notification body).
evidence: in-page repro output: lone surrogate 0xd83d, encodeURIComponent throws (tmp-20-t5 stdout)
issues.recommendation: Truncate with Array.from(name).slice(0,24).join('') or Intl.Segmenter to respect code points/graphemes.
